The actual run of descent PUZZLES is four: sh, s3, o4, s5.

Verified true: docs/design/rooms-v2-passability.json gives switchback-spine-a west->ceiling = 371 at `none`, which is indeed the 2nd longest `none` pair route in the whole set (antiphase-airlock-c east->west 392 is 1st; next is metronome-gallery-c 287). docs/design/rooms-v2-metadata.json does say the route "already uses 371" against a ~600-tick horizon and that a missed hop "demotes you to the bottom run and you walk the whole spine again". docs/design/dungeon-v2-rationale.md line 97 does label `swb` easy.

Refutation: the 371-tick bare ascent is unreachable in the actual dungeon, so it is not "the longest bare traversal on any route". In docs/design/dungeon-v2-layout.txt, swb has exactly two doors: `edge lcc east swb west` and `edge sb2 floor swb ceiling`. So a west->ceiling ascent must come through lcc (low-ceiling-arena-c), which itself has only two entries:
- `edge kv east lcc west`, explicitly dash-gated (`gate kv east ability dash`), and lcc west->east is null at `none`/`wall` anyway (dash/both only, 101).

The `none` column for this room is a solver capability figure, not a figure any player experiences on route; the rationale's own Act ordering puts the southern loop entirely post-boots ("the keyhole vault's east door opens into low-ceiling-arena-c's dash pinches, closing the big southern loop").

The double-seal is an explicit, documented design intent, not an oversight: rationale line 36-37 — "The boots vault is now reachable from either side (metronome corridor above, shutter-chute climb below)". Two-sided approach to a key-item vault is standard practice, not a halved promise. rejected.title: kv east dash-gate voids keyhole-vault-a's documented no-trap contract
rejected.note:
Refuted. The passability facts cited are accurate (keyhole-vault-a `west->ceiling` is null at every loadout, `east->ceiling` solves only at `both`, and the layout does put `gate kv east ability dash` on one side door), but the softlock conclusion does not follow once you trace who can actually be standing in kv.

Every entrance into kv already implies dash or glove:

1. `edge t1 floor kv ceiling` (the one-way funnel). To reach t1 you must pass s1 floor -> o2 ceiling -> o2 floor. one-way-loop-b `ceiling->floor` is {both: 128, dash: null, none: null, wall: null} — only a glove+boots player can descend that shaft. Such a player has dash, so `gate kv east ability dash` opens. A bare player physically cannot reach t1/kv from above.
2. `edge kv east lcc west` is itself the dash gate, so anyone arriving from the east has dash.
3. `edge tc east kv west`. tc is reachable only from s5 east, and s5 is reachable only via o4 floor. o4 (`one-way-loop-b`) `ceiling->floor` again needs `both`; the other way in is `o4 east` behind `gate o4 east ability wall`, i.e. glove. The file itself documents Inconclusive as "never a proof that the [pair] is unreachable".

(2) The `wall` loadout is a strict superset of `none` in the simulation. In crates/downwards-core/src/simulation.rs, abilities.wall_jump only gates additional behaviour: begin_wall_jump (~lines 868, 987) and wall_sliding (line 952). Wall-sliding further requires holding into the wall (effective_move_x == side.direction()), which is optional and positionally free when flush against a wall. Hence the 106-tick `none` solution is physically executable at `wall`; the climb is not impossible at any loadout.

(3) Even granting the premise, no softlock follows. bv has two doors (`edge bv floor sh ceiling`, `edge bv east met west`), both gated on the same wall ability. The critique's own run reaches bv via the met corridor, which is bidirectional and already unlocked at that point, so the player enters and exits bv with boots. Descent bv->sh is unaffected (ceiling->floor 92, floor->floor 8 solve at every loadout including wall).

(4) python3 tools/dungeon_layout_metrics.py docs/design/dungeon-v2-layout.txt reports still-locked-doors-at-end 0 and verdict ok.

REFUTED on its core claim, though its two factual sub-claims check out.

What holds: in docs/design/dungeon-v2-layout.txt, `br` (braided-crossing-a) appears exactly once, on the o2→br→ga2 spur, and `tc` (two-clock-fork-b) exactly once, on `s5 east tc west` / `tc east kv west`, behind `gate s5 floor ability dash` and hard strata-sort-c. Neither sits on the s1→ap→gb→t2→oc→sb2→crown line. dungeon_layout_metrics reports edge-disjoint-spawn-goal-routes 1, so that line is essentially forced.

What breaks it: "the only two genuine multi-solution classes" is false against docs/design/rooms-v2-metadata.json, and the counterexample is the spawn room itself.
- strata-sort-a (`s1`, the spawn, plus `sa2`), ability_requirement "none": "both lanes reach both exits, so the choice is pure risk/reward — a near-aligned left lane is a spike-fringed freefall to the bottom-left chamber, while the braided right lane costs a walk on every stratum but is spike-free and carries both easy coins." That is exactly the risky-fast vs safe-slow-with-different-reward structure the finding says exists only at br and tc, and the player meets it in room one, on the critical path.
- antiphase-airlock-a (`ap`), the very corridor the fix proposes to add variety to, already carries a second solution: "a sealed dash-crawl vent lane above the chambers offers an untimed express route that can never bank" — timed-walk vs untimed-but-unbankable.
- keyhole-vault-a (`kv`) is a third: "priced rather than gated — a no-ability stair on the right buys the east door cheaply... while a 60px bare-walled shaft on the left sells the same west exit for three moves to anyone carrying a glove or boots."
- low-ceiling-arena-b (`lcb`) offers dash-pinch vs lap-the-building for the same traverse.

Also worth noting the finding overstates tc's own credentials relative to br: two-clock-fork-b's high lane is "behind a one-tile dash-crawl slot" and is described as "the dash-gated high lane", so it is not two ability-free lanes the way braided-crossing-a is.

Net: the placement observation about br and tc is accurate, but the "only two" framing that makes it a major variety defect is contradicted by the metadata, and the suggested fix targets a corridor (`ap → gb`) whose room already contains a two-lane choice. At most this is a minor note about depth-of-placement, not a major variety finding.
